name: Add streaming parse for large JSON
description: Add a parseJsonStream function that parses large JSON files incrementally without loading entire file into memory. Returns async iterator of parsed objects.
setup: const testPath = path.join(workspace, 'test-stream.js'); fs.writeFileSync(testPath, `import test from 'ava'; import { parseJsonStream } from './index.js'; import fs from 'fs'; test('parseJsonStream parses large JSON array incrementally', async t => { const largeArray = '[' + Array(1000).fill('{"value":1}').join(',') + ']'; fs.writeFileSync('temp-large.json', largeArray); const results = []; for await (const item of parseJsonStream(fs.createReadStream('temp-large.json'))) { results.push(item); } t.is(results.length, 1000); fs.unlinkSync('temp-large.json'); }); test('parseJsonStream handles malformed JSON gracefully', async t => { const badJson = '{"a":1}\n{"b":}'; fs.writeFileSync('temp-bad.json', badJson); const results = []; for await (const item of parseJsonStream(fs.createReadStream('temp-bad.json'))) { results.push(item); } t.is(results.length, 1); fs.unlinkSync('temp-bad.json'); }); `);
verify: const indexPath = path.join(workspace, 'index.js'); if (!fs.existsSync(indexPath)) return false; const content = fs.readFileSync(indexPath, 'utf8'); return content.includes('parseJsonStream') && content.includes('export');
